chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who permits his slave to marry a free woman or a slave girl of a people; is the divorce right with the master or with the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: The divorce is with the slave.

key_terms.أَمَةَ قَوْمٍ: A slave girl belonging to a people/family

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to divorce when a slave maries with his master's permission?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) clarifies that a male slave retains the independent right to initiate divorce (*talaq*) over his wife, whether she is a free woman or a slave, provided he married with his master's permission. This ruling underscores the slave's legal agency in personal status matters, distinguishing his marital authority from the master's ownership rights, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding *mukatab* and non-*mukatab* slaves.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the man who permits his slave that he marries the free woman, or a slave girl, would the divorced be fixed to the master or to the slave?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The divorce is up to the slave’.
